survivors.reason: The instruction explicitly specifies budget_weight=1 in the public AddDPNoiseParams constructor. This mutant instead defaults it to 2, so a caller omitting the argument obtains params.budget_weight==2 and the retained engine passes 2 into the accountant scope and _compute_budgets_for_aggregation. This is a direct observable API-contract violation, even though a single aggregation can receive the same normalized total budget. The grader never asserts the default: its only two-session weighted test explicitly supplies budget_weight=1 and budget_weight=2, so that test bypasses the mutation. The bound full=1/nop=0 and mutant=1 headers establish a scored survivor; the constructor/forwarding counterexample is source reasoning, not a fresh control. block.label: out_of_scope
block.reason: The issue is a TradingClient.close_all_positions response ValidationError, with False explicitly supplied in the reproduction and True in the traceback. The kept model definitions make all four missing FailedClosePositionDetails fields optional. Earlier float annotations left above them are overwritten by the later same-name annotations/defaults in the Python class body, so removing those duplicates is not required. The omitted client defaults and omission of false-valued request dictionaries are separate API/request-construction changes; the supplied calls do not omit cancel_orders. The two selected grader tests exercise partial code/message response bodies with False and both pass. This omission therefore does not leave the reported parsing defect unfixed. It is distinct from the Trading line mutant that newly discards an explicitly True cancellation request.
